instruction: I don't want websites to access my location. Can you block all websites from requesting location access in Chrome?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"profile":{"content_settings":{"exceptions":{"geolocation":{}}}}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to block geolocation/location tracking in Chrome. The evaluator checks profile.content_settings.exceptions.geolocation for default block setting. Initial state: no geolocation blocks. Expected: geolocation blocked (setting=2). Getter returns 'true' when blocked.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and navigates to profile.content_settings.exceptions.geolocation
Getter correctly checks the default setting '*,*' which represents all websites
Getter correctly interprets setting values (1=allow, 2=block) and returns 'true' when blocked, 'false' otherwise
Metric 'exact_match' appropriately compares the getter result with expected value 'true'
Instruction requirement 'block all websites from requesting location access' is fully covered by checking the default geolocation setting
Data flow is correct: getter extracts setting value → returns string 'true'/'false' → metric compares with expected 'true'
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure fresh state for verification
Expected value 'true' is semantically correct for the task of blocking geolocation
